title: Decoding certificates
purpose: Decodes a certificate or a chain bundle, PEM or DER: subject, issuer, SANs, serial, how many days it has left, its key, its signature algorithm, its basic constraints and key usage, and its fingerprints, so a TLS failure can be explained from the files. It never connects to the host.
inputs: A certificate file in the workspace, stdin, or `--text`, and optionally `--host` to ask whether the first certificate's SANs cover that host.
verifies: The bundle is checked as a chain in the order given: each certificate's issuer must be the next one's subject, and its signature must verify with the next one's key. Expired and not-yet-valid certificates are flagged, toil's DER reader is held against Node's, and an out-of-order bundle gets the order that fixes it.
limits: Nothing is checked against a trust store, and a root that isn't in the bundle is `UNVERIFIED`. A private key is never read. PKCS#7 and PKCS#12 files aren't read, and `--host` uses SANs only, never the subject CN.
